meta.description: An atlas of Indian mythology, cosmology, genealogy and sacred geography.

notice.contentEnglish: Descriptions, explanations and source passages are currently shown in English. Names appear in Devanagari where available.

search.title: Search
search.intro: English, Hindi (Devanagari) or IAST — diacritics optional.
search.label: Search
search.results: {count, plural, one {# result} other {# results}} for “{query}”

view.label: View
view.noWebgl: 3D needs WebGL, which this browser does not provide

time.title: Time
time.cosmicNote: Positions inside a tradition’s cycle of ages. Not years.
time.historicalNote: Academic dates from evidence. A different system: not comparable.

verified.label: Historically verified
verified.explain: Supported by archaeological or historical evidence. This does not verify the stories set here.

traditional.label: Traditionally identified
traditional.explain: Located here by living tradition; not independently verified.

debated.label: Debated
debated.explain: Scholars and traditions propose different locations.

mythical.label: Cosmological
mythical.explain: A realm of the cosmos, not a place on Earth. It has no map position.

public_domain.label: Public domain
public_domain.explain: May be quoted with a citation.

open_licence.label: Open licence
open_licence.explain: May be quoted under its licence.

cited_only.label: Cited only
cited_only.explain: Still in copyright somewhere. KĀLA cites it by page but never reproduces it.

kingdomKind.epic_legendary: Kingdom of the epics and Puranas

variantTag.title: This claim belongs to one account; other accounts may differ.

variantPanel.heading: Different texts, different accounts
variantPanel.body: Some of the connections below come from one particular account. Other texts may tell it differently.
variantPanel.shared: {count, plural, one {# connection is} other {# connections are}} shared across the sources KĀLA holds.

place.modernBorders: Modern borders are shown for orientation. They do not mean the ancient place belonged to a modern country.

kingdom.sameNameLegendary: A historical state of the same name is documented separately. Sharing a name does not make the epic account historical.
kingdom.sameNameHistorical: The epics and Puranas describe a kingdom of the same name. That account is kept separately and is not confirmed by this historical record.

variant.oneAccountBody: This is how one text or tradition describes the beginning. Others describe it differently; none is presented here as the single true account.
variant.continueGenealogy: Continue: the families of gods and sages →

event.whereNote: A place being real does not make the event historical.

concept.schoolsNote: These traditions do not always agree. Each explanation is given on its own terms and sourced to its own texts.

network.seeOnMap: See these places on the map →
network.moreBody: Texts and traditions give different lists for this network. Each list is shown on its own; none is presented as the only one.

opening.line3: Before the stories of gods and mortals —
opening.title: KĀLA — an atlas of Indian mythology, cosmology, genealogy and sacred geography
opening.pathwaysIntro: Hymns, philosophies and Puranas each give their own account of how things began. KĀLA keeps them side by side. Choose one to begin.

cosmic.intro: Many Hindu texts describe time as cycles of ages (yugas) nested inside larger cycles. Different texts give different figures, so each account is shown on its own.
cosmic.notice: Traditional chronology, not historical dating. These cycles cannot be placed on a calendar of years BCE/CE.
cosmic.nonePlaced: No figures or events are placed in this yuga in KĀLA’s content yet.
cosmic.prompt: Select a yuga on the wheel or with the buttons to see its length and what the texts place in it.
cosmic.innerText: one mahayuga = {years} divine years, split into four yugas.
cosmic.middleText: one manvantara (age of a Manu) = {count} mahayugas.
cosmic.outerUndivided: this text does not state how many manvantaras make a kalpa, so the ring is left undivided.
cosmic.outerStated: The text gives {count} mahayugas for a day of Brahma.
cosmic.tableCaption: The four yugas of one mahayuga, in divine years

genealogy.intro: Families of gods, sages, beings and kings, as the texts describe them. Every line is a connection a source makes. Where texts disagree, each account is kept and labelled.
genealogy.accountsNote: Claims that belong to one text can be hidden. Claims shared across the sources are always shown.
genealogy.prompt: Select a figure — click a star, use the list, or search — to see its card and trace its connections.
genealogy.none: No connection found in the accounts shown. KĀLA only links figures where a source makes the connection.

geography.intro: Sacred and ancient places, each marked with how confident the identification is. A place being real does not make the stories set there historical.
geography.hintMythological: Places the texts connect to stories, figures or legendary kingdoms. Positions in story time, not dates.
geography.hintHistorical: Places with archaeological or historical evidence, or a historical state. Dated by evidence.
geography.lensNote: Story time and historical dates are different systems and are never placed on one timeline.
geography.modernNote: Modern names and borders are shown for orientation only. They are never projected back onto ancient places.
geography.prompt: Select a place on the globe or in the list.
geography.notOnMapBody: Cosmological realms are part of the cosmos the texts describe, not places on Earth. They have no coordinates.
geography.proposedLegend: Proposed location of a debated place
